name: Bourns-mfmsmf
title: MF-MSMF series: 0.10 A to 3.00 A hold, 6 V to 60 V polymer PTC resettable fuses in 1812
summary: A family of 52 polymer PTC resettable fuses on the 1812 (4532 metric) footprint, holding 0.10 A to 3.00 A at 23 °C with maximum voltages from 6 V to 60 V. Each one carries its hold current at low resistance and switches to a high-resistance tripped state on an overcurrent or overtemperature fault, then resets once the fault is removed. Models with an X suffix are the freeXpansion design (outline Style 2); the plain models (Style 1) are still sold but are not recommended for new designs. All models carry cUL and TÜV recognition and most are AEC-Q200 compliant. Named uses include USB 2.0, USB 3.0 and OTG ports, HDMI 1.4 sources, PC motherboards and peripherals, hard disk drives, PCMCIA cards, point-of-sale equipment and server and data-centre interfaces.
key_figures: Rmin 0.010 Ω to 0.70 Ω; R1max 0.040 Ω to 15 Ω

notes: An order code is MF-MSMF, then the hold current in hundredths of an ampere (010 for 0.10 A up to 300 for 3.00 A), then /voltage rating where one is given (6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 30, 33, 40, 48 or 60 V), then X for the freeXpansion design or nothing for the standard design, then -2 for tape and reel to EIA-481.
MSMF stands for the 4532 metric (1812 inch) surface-mount body.

Style 1 parts are marked with the part code, a one-digit year code (5 = 2025) and a bi-weekly date code letter (Y = weeks 49-50); MF-MSMF020/60 carries its part code 2 alone. Style 2 parts carry the one-character part code above a bi-weekly date code letter (C = weeks 5-6).
The marking entry MF-260/8X & 260/12X = Y should read MF-MSMF260/8X & 260/12X = Y.

operation.text: Each model is a polymer positive-temperature-coefficient resettable fuse for overcurrent and overtemperature protection. At 23 °C in still air it carries its hold current for 30 minutes without tripping, and its resistance lies within Rmin and R1max. A fault at or above the trip current trips it to a high resistance; the higher the fault current, the shorter the time to trip, and the curves give typical values at 23 °C. It resets once the fault is removed.

Hold current falls as ambient temperature rises and rises as it falls; the derating table gives Ihold for each model from -40 °C to 85 °C. MF-MSMF010, for example, holds 0.16 A at -40 °C, 0.10 A at 23 °C and 0.03 A at 85 °C.

Models without an X suffix are built in outline Style 1, which has terminals wrapping the two ends on both faces and no D maximum or E dimension. X-suffix models are the freeXpansion design in outline Style 2: the top face carries the marking and the terminal bands are on the bottom face. Both styles use electroless nickel under immersion gold (ENIG) on the terminals.

Running a part past its maximum voltage or current can damage it and can lead to arcing or fire. Inductance in the protected circuit can raise the voltage across the part above its rating, so such circuits need evaluating in the application. The parts protect against temporary overcurrent or overtemperature up to their rated limits, not against overcurrent or overvoltage that is expected to repeat or persist.

The polymer swells when it trips, so the part needs free space around it and must not be held rigidly; hard potting or tight housings can stop it working. Lubricants, silicone oils, solvents, gels, electrolytes and acids can degrade it. Conformal coatings, potting and sealing compounds can carry strong solvents such as xylene or toluene, which must be fully cured or baked out of the part. Store at +40 °C max and 70 % relative humidity max.

The parts are made for reflow soldering by hot plate, hot air, infrared, nitrogen or vapour phase, with Pb or Pb-free solder. Wave soldering is allowed only with the part on the top of the board, away from the solder wave; hand soldering is not recommended. A reflow above the profile can leave the part outside its published figures. Too much solder can bridge the terminals.

cUL file E174545 and TÜV certificate R50256634 cover every model; the TÜV approval is to IEC 62319-1, IEC 60738-1 and IEC 60730-1:2013 clauses 15 and 17 and Annex J. The parts are RoHS compliant to Directive 2015/863 and halogen free, which Bourns defines as bromine 900 ppm max, chlorine 900 ppm max and the two together 1500 ppm max. They carry a California Proposition 65 warning for lead.
